frame.title: Colonies
frame._note: One PNG with transparent cutouts, stretched over the 1920x1080 reference area and drawn above all content. Every box in boxes.json is derived from the cutouts by tools/frame_holes.py (--write regenerates them). Do not move the cutout boxes by hand. The frame was generated at 1672x941 and is upscaled at every resolution; if the metal reads soft next to the galaxy map, regenerate the art larger and re-run frame_holes.
frame._title_note: The original has no title on this screen; the cutout is the same title bar the galaxy map has, so it carries the screen name.

sort._note: The seven sort buttons of the original (colsum.cpp:267-273, Add_Multi_Button_Field_ at y=446). TWO ways in, and the hotkey is the one taken: `hotkey` is the original's own binding (ESTR 384/…: n p f i s r b), sent as INJECT_KEY, which moves nothing else. `native_click` is a point inside each native button and STAYS - as the fallback, and because it is the checkable one: the point comes from the Add_Multi_Button_Field_ call above and can be verified by a grep with no game running. A click also drags the game's own pointer onto the button (platform.cpp:1171-1172); the key does not. Second source for the hotkeys, live 3 September 2026 on orion2re 1.60: the FIELD_LIST reports fields 16-22 at y 446-469 carrying N P F I S R B - the same seven letters, UPPERCASE on the wire, and the game accepts either case.

return.label: Return
return._note: colsum.cpp:265 Add_Button_Field_(531, 445, …). The CLICK path, not the sort bar's hotkey path: RETURN has no letter to press. Its field (id 14, read live 3 September 2026) reports a hotkey byte of 0x25, which is not a key a player is asked for, so this button keeps its native_click and _inject falls through to it.

empire._note: VERSION: every file:line in this block was read in orion2re 1.60 (src/version.h). A 1.31 archive numbers them differently - Draw_Empire_Info_ is at 408 there, not 418. Transcribed from COLSUM::Draw_Empire_Info_ (colsum.cpp:418): six lines printed at native (520, 354), each an ESTRING with one s_player field. signed=true prints an explicit plus like the original's %+d. Draw order, labels and ESTR ids are the original's and are load-bearing - see _estrings_note, _join_note, _justify_note and _geometry_note.
empire._estrings_note: Read in orion2re 1.60. The six ESTR ids, in the order Draw_Empire_Info_ passes them, with the string as orion2_str.h records it. THE STRINGS ARE NOT IN THE SOURCE: ESTRINGS::Load_E_Strings_ (estrings.cpp:11) loads them at runtime from the player's own estrings.lbx (or estrGERM/FREN/SPAN/ITAL/POLI by settings.language), so E_Strings_(n) is an index into LBX data. orion2_str.h is the second-best thing - the enum carries each string as a comment - and that is where these came from. || 118 ESTR_SRESERVE_SD '%sReserve: %s%d' | 106 ESTR_SINCOME_SSD '%sIncome: %s%s%+d' | 114 ESTR_SPOPULATION_SD '%sPopulation: %s%d' | 103 ESTR_SFREIGHTERS_SD '%sFreighters: %s%d' | 102 ESTR_SFOOD_SD '%sFood: %s%+d' | 117 ESTR_SRESEARCH_SD '%sResearch: %s%d'. THE SIGN IS NOT DECORATION: only Income (106) and Food (102) carry %+d, the other four are plain %d, which is why 'signed' is per row here and not a screen-wide setting. RESEARCH IS ABSOLUTE AND CARRIES NO PERCENT - and the reason is worth stating because it is easy to cite wrongly: 117 is '%sResearch: %s%d', there is no %% in it and none in any research label. The only entries in the whole table with a literal %% are 108 (maintenance penalty), 112 (morale), 120 and 121 (worker penalty), plus HESTR 0x142 '-%d%% prod'.
empire._colour_note: CORRECTED 2 September 2026, and the correction matters. This note first said the two per-line prefixes were COLOUR attributes, label and value. In orion2re 1.60 they are NOT. ESTRINGS::s_0_0055110c and s_1_00551110 (estrings.cpp:8-9) are the C literals "\0320" and "\0321", and those compile to the bytes 1A 30 and 1A 31 - octal 032 is 0x1A, not ESC. FMTPARA dispatches 0x1A to Set_Justification_ and 0x1B to Set_Current_Colors_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368), so the two prefixes are JUSTIFICATION codes. Only the red one is a colour: ERIC::Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:176) returns "\0332" = bytes 1B 32 = Set_Current_Colors_('2'), which sets color_attr = code << 5 (fmtpara.cpp:1154). THE PART THAT SURVIVES UNCHANGED: red-if-negative is the original's and applies to Income ALONE - Food is signed but never turns red, however negative it gets, and warn_negative on any other row is an HD EXTENSION (see _warn_negative_note). THE PART THAT DID NOT: there is no per-line label colour and no per-line value colour in 1.60. A 1.31 archive was cited as having \0330 and \0331, which WOULD be ESC and WOULD be colours; that has not been checked against a 1.31 tree and is exactly the kind of difference this version tag exists to expose.
empire._red_note: CHECKED AND KEPT, after a query that it might rest on a mis-transcribed byte. It does not. ERIC::Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:176) returns the literal "\0332", and a C octal escape is greedy to three digits: \033 is 0x1B (ESC), leaving '2' as a plain character, so the bytes are 1B 32 and FMTPARA routes 0x1B to Set_Current_Colors_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368, :1154). Three things agree: the bytes, the function's own comment ('ESC + 2 emits a text-attribute control sequence'), and colsum.cpp itself, which spells the same effect "\x1B" "2" at :567, :575 and :1189. Contrast the JUSTIFICATION pair, where "\0320" takes \032 = 0x1A - same-looking literal, one octal digit apart, opposite meaning. That is the trap, and it is on the other pair. What IS open about these symbols is an array size, not a value: see _open_note.
empire._warn_negative_note: HD EXTENSION on two of the three rows that carry it. The original turns exactly one line red, Income, via Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ on surplus_bc (eric.cpp:176) - Food is printed with an explicit sign but in the value colour however negative it is, and Freighters has neither sign nor colour. This screen colours all three, because a negative food or freighter balance is the same class of fact as a negative income and the original's restraint there is a 16-colour-palette economy rather than a judgement. Income is TRANSCRIBED; food and freighters are the extension.
empire._open_note: TWO OPEN ITEMS, both read in orion2re 1.60. (1) THE ATTRIBUTE SYMBOLS ARE DECLARED AT TWO SIZES AND DEFINED THREE TIMES. colsum.h:87-88 and strings.h:39-40 declare s_0_0055110c and s_1_00551110 as const char[3]; estrings.h:9-10 declares the same names const char[4]. There are three definitions in three namespaces - COLSUM (colsum.cpp:36-37, [3], octal), ESTRINGS (estrings.cpp:8-9, [4], octal) and strings (strings.cpp:22,24, [3], hex). All three produce the same bytes, so nothing misbehaves today, and the VALUE is not in doubt. The declaration disagreement is, and it is a question for Joes rather than a fix request: see doc/orion2re_open_fixes.md. (2) E_Strings_(12) has no entry in orion2_str.h - no name, no comment - so its text is unknown and only its USES can be read. Every use in the tree is consistent with the empty string: button and hotkey labels where the sprite carries the artwork (colsum.cpp:263-302, colbldg.cpp:346-364), 'no help text' (colsysdi.cpp:212), 'no prefix' (colsum.cpp:563 when a star is not blockaded), and the not-negative branch of Red_If_Negative_Fmt_String_ (eric.cpp:178). Consistent is not confirmed. Nothing here depends on it; the 'Buy' label in list._buy_note is a word this project chose precisely because 12 could not supply one.
empire._join_note: Read in orion2re 1.60. The six are built into ONE buffer and printed once. ERIC::String_Builder2_ (eric.cpp:425) formats each line, then for build_mode != 0 joins it to what is already there with snprintf(dest, size, E_Strings_(71), existing, 13, new) - E_Strings_(71) is '%s%c%s' and the character is the literal 13. So the separator is a CARRIAGE RETURN, not a newline, and the whole block reaches FMTPARA::Print_Formatted_Paragraph_ as a single string.
empire._justify_note: SETTLED, and it reverses what this note said twice before. THE LAYOUT: each entry is ONE row, label LEFT and value RIGHT. The two per-line prefixes are justification codes - s_0_0055110c is the bytes 1A 30 = Set_Justification_('0') and s_1_00551110 is 1A 31 = Set_Justification_('1'), and FMTPARA routes 0x1A to Set_Justification_ (fmtpara.cpp:364-368). Justify_Line_ (fmtpara.cpp:1699) implements mode 1 by adding the whole remaining width to the first character's advance, which is right alignment; the right edge is para.x2 = x + width - 1 = 623 of 640 (fmtpara.cpp:657). ONE ROW AND NOT TWO: Set_Justification_ (fmtpara.cpp:999) flushes the pending segment through Complete_Line_ when char_count > 0 but never advances y - y moves only on CR, LF, VT and FF (fmtpara.cpp:322-341, where CR falls through to Vertical_Move_Line_Advance_). The CR that String_Builder2_ joins the six with is what ends each row. WHY justify=3 IS INERT, corrected: not because CR terminates each line, though it would also do that. The buffer BEGINS with s_0, so the very first thing the parser meets is Set_Justification_('0') with char_count still 0 - it skips the flush entirely and assigns justify_mode = 0 (fmtpara.cpp:1017). Mode 3 is overwritten before a single character is drawn and never reaches Justify_Line_. WHY THIS WAS WRONG TWICE: an octal 032 read as 033. '\0320' looks like ESC + '0' and is SUB + '0' - a C octal escape is greedy to three digits, so \032 = 0x1A, not \033 = 0x1B. Read as ESC it is a colour code and the six lines are plain left-aligned text; read correctly it is a justification code and the original does label-left/value-right. The 1.60 tree settles it three ways: two files spell the pair '\0320'/'\0321' (colsum.cpp:36-37, estrings.cpp:8-9) and a third spells it '\x1A' '0' / '\x1A' '1' (strings.cpp:22, :24) - unambiguous, and commented in the source itself as 'switches paragraph justification to left alignment' and 'to right alignment'. THE INVENTION IS NOW THE OTHER WAY ROUND: label-left/value-right is the TRANSCRIPTION and is what this screen draws; the stacked, centred label-over-value it drew until 2 September 2026 was the invention.
empire._geometry_note: Read in orion2re 1.60. Native, 640x480, for anyone re-deriving the HD boxes. The empire paragraph: x 520, y 354, width 104 (colsum.cpp:418, Print_Formatted_Paragraph_). The colony rows, from Draw_Colony_Summary_For_Colony_ (colsum.cpp:538): row y = list_idx * 0x1F + 0x26, so slot * 31 + 38; the name column is Squeeze_Formatted_Paragraph_Centered_(0x0C, y, w, 0x17) - x 12, height 23, width 0x59 = 89 normally and 0x57 = 87 when the colony has an event, because the event label takes the two px; the building column is Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16) - x 512, width 85, height 22.
empire._native_width_note: DEVIATION, live at every resolution. The width of the original's empire paragraph in its own 640x480 pixels: Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(520, 354, 104, buffer, 3) at colsum.cpp:418, read in orion2re 1.60. The right edge of a VALUE is x + width - 1 = 623 (para.x2, fmtpara.cpp:657), and THAT alignment is transcribed. The WIDTH is not: 104 scaled by REF_W / 640 is 312 reference px against the 286 the sidebar cutout gives, so screen.py clamps to the cutout and the clamp fires everywhere. 286 against 312 is 8.3 % of the column - every value sits 26 reference px left of the original's proportion. Both numbers are kept and the clamp is a min() rather than a hardcoded 286 so that it stops firing by itself if the frame art ever gives this hole 312 or more; the art is NOT being changed to suit it. A smoke check asserts this key is still read and still larger than what is drawn, so it cannot be deleted as dead weight once somebody notices it never wins.

panels._note: Every cutout that shows content gets the panel fill, so the frame never sits over raw background. list_area draws the colony list (see `list`) and output_panel the original's scan box for the selected colony (see `output`); galaxy_inset and spare_panel are still fill only. WHICH HOLE IS WHICH IS DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE, not from left-to-right position - until 4 September 2026 frame_holes.py assigned these three names by index and had the last two the wrong way round. galaxy_inset is the RIGHTMOST of the three and is the original's own map hole: MOVEBOX::Draw_Galaxy_Map_Box_(nullptr, 0, 0x17c, 0x15d, 0x80, 0x5b, ...) at colsum.cpp:415 draws the small galaxy map at native (380, 349, 128, 91) (movebox.cpp:4-9), which is reference (1140, 785, 384, 205), centre x 1332. spare_panel is the MIDDLE one, over native x ~193-347, where the original draws its production and morale sprite column (Draw_Colony_Wee_Prod_(..., 106, y_pos, 366, 20), colsum.cpp:1171-1176) - values output_panel already answers for, which is what makes that hole the spare rather than a second place to draw the same thing. A smoke check asserts the rule (nearest hole to the native rect must be the one named galaxy_inset, and decisively nearest) rather than the list, so a re-generated frame cannot quietly reassign the names again. ONE PANEL PER STEP - the two that are empty are empty on purpose and not waiting on anything in this file.

list._invention: INVENTION. The original draws three columns of population sprites per row, one icon per colonist, squished when a colony outgrows its column (COLDRAW::Do_Colony_Info_Pop_Stuff_For_Pop_, coldraw.cpp:282; Calculate_Squish_Step_, coldraw.cpp:12). This draws one allocation bar per row instead: one square per colonist, three zones in ECON order. MOO2 could not draw it and does not. Marked here, in colonylist.py (the renderer), in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.
list._transcribed: The row set (colonies whose owner is the local player), the zone order food/industry/research (ECON_FOOD=0, orion2_consts.h:119; the original's own column order, colsum.cpp:318-329), the 'No Farming' label and the condition max_farms == 0 that shows it (coldraw.cpp:315, ESTR_NO_FARMING 387), and the bar length, which is COLCALC::Planet_Max_Population_For_Player_ (colcalc.cpp:896) and never _planet_max_population[size] alone. The TRACK length is transcribed too, and separately: it is the engine's own population ceiling (POP_LIMIT_CAP in colonyrows.py, which carries its three sources — s_colony.pop[], the clamp at the end of COLCALC::Planet_Max_Population_For_Player_ colcalc.cpp:930, and the per-job cap in COLMOVE::Give_Colonist_New_Job_ colmove.cpp:518). The number lives in that constant and nowhere else, here included.
list._overflow_note: THE LIST DROPS ROWS THAT DO NOT FIT, and until 3 September 2026 it did so in silence. render() stops at the first row that would cross the bottom of list_area; at 1920x1080 the panel holds NINE rows, and a twelve-colony empire therefore lost three with nothing on screen saying so. Every drawn row was correct and every check in the suite was green, because every check looked at rows that were drawn - the fault was found by somebody noticing a colony they owned was missing from a screenshot. The wording lives here per decision 15 and {count} is substituted by replace, not str.format (decision 37). Setting it to the empty string restores the silent behaviour, which is worth knowing and is not worth doing. THIS IS NOT A SCROLLBAR AND NOT A STEP TOWARDS ONE. What scrolling should look like has its own source - the original windows ten rows over the sorted list (Update_Col_List_, colsum.cpp:348) and resets _first on every sort click (colsum.cpp:828) - and that is a separate decision, taken on its own evidence rather than under the pressure of a visible bug. What this does is turn a silence into a state, the same rule the dimmed Producing header follows.
list._no_farming_note: Drawn BELOW the bar, in the band row_height already pays for: row_height 58 against bar_height 30 leaves 28 px, split 14 above and 14 below by centring the bar, and the label renders 88x14. It used to sit in a horizontal tail_width column, which cost 150 px of the shared budget for a label most rows do not show. no_farming_placement 'tail' restores the old position. The first version drew it at the bar's LEFT EDGE, inside the track, and the worker squares painted straight over it: every number correct, nothing on screen. Below the bar is outside the track's band by construction — squares occupy y+1 to y+bar_height-1 — so a full 42-slot row cannot reach it. That is a property of the geometry rather than of the data, and the smoke test asserts it against a row with all 42 slots filled.
list._track_note: The track is always POP_LIMIT_CAP slots long — the engine's population ceiling, defined once in colonyrows.py with its sources and its reasons — so one square is the same size in every row and in every empire. Three regions per row: filled (zone colour), free (dashed outline, reachable today), unreachable (a faint baseline only, reachable later via Advanced City Planning, Biospheres, Subterranean and terraforming). The third is not padding.
list._tail_width_note: 0 today. This reserved a column to the RIGHT of the track for the 'No Farming' label; the label moved into the spare height under the bar on 1 September 2026 and the 150 px went back to the slot, taking unit from 19 to 22. Kept as a key, not deleted: it is also the reservation a building column will take, and _horizontal_budget is costed in those terms. Setting it non-zero narrows the track by exactly that much.
list._horizontal_budget: THE ONE BUDGET. list_area is 1408 reference px and every column spends from it. The column sum - name_width + (building_width + building_gap) + 2*pad_x + 42*unit + 41*square_gap - balances at scale 1.0, and at fractional scales it does not: unit is a floor division and the six terms are each truncated by int() independently, so between 11 and 30 px go missing. The renderer hands that remainder to the name column's DRAWN width, which makes the sum balance BY CONSTRUCTION at every resolution and therefore worthless as a check - a thing that cannot fail asserts nothing. What is asserted instead, across twelve window sizes rather than the two keys in boxes.json, is the pair the construction can still get wrong: building_right + pad_x == list_area.right, and the ellipsis threshold being the same reference-px value everywhere. See _name_width_note for why the remainder is gutter and not text budget. Fixed: pad_x 22 twice = 44, plus 41 inter-slot gaps of square_gap 2 = 82, so 126. building_width also takes building_gap 16 when non-zero. unit = (1408 - name_width - tail_width - (building_width + 16) - 126) // 42, and the shipped values are chosen so that division is EXACT: (1408 - 236 - 0 - 206 - 44 - 82) / 42 = 840 / 42 = 20, remainder 0. Measured at 1920x1080, scale 1.0. || name_width | no building col | + building 190 || 330: 22 | 17 || 240: 24 | 19 || 236: 24 | 20. SHIPPED: name_width 236 with the 190 column, unit 20. WHY 236 AND NOT 240: until 2 September 2026 it was 240 and the divide FLOORED - 836/42 = 19.905 became unit 19, and 240 + 206 + 44 + 798 + 82 came to 1370 against 1408. The 38 px the floor threw away were not spent anywhere; they sat as dead air between the right edge of the building column (1446) and the right edge of list_area (1506), which is where a 60 px gap after the Buy buttons came from. Four px off the name column buys the exact divide, a 20 px square instead of 19, and a row that ends flush: slot 42 at 1278, building column 1294 to 1484, right pad_x to 1506. 236 still holds the realistic maximum of 230 - see _name_width_note. The earlier '190 is unaffordable, it needs 315' was wrong - it came from measuring a one-line full-font worst case the original never imposes. See _building_column_note.
list._name_width_note: 236, and IT IS THE TEXT BUDGET, NOT THE COLUMN WIDTH. The drawn column is this times the scale PLUS a per-resolution remainder - the pixels the slot's floor division drops, which the renderer adds to this column and to nothing else so the row ends flush at the panel edge (30 px at 1280x720, 15 at 2560x1440, 0 at scale 1.0 and 2.0). That remainder is GUTTER between the name and the first slot. It never becomes room for text: the name right-aligns, clips and ellipsises against name_width * scale alone, so the threshold stays 244 reference px at every resolution instead of ranging 244 to 288 and cutting the same name on one monitor but not another. Nothing is written back here - the remainder is computed per frame in track_metrics and stored nowhere. The four px between this and the 240 it was until 2 September 2026 are not a measurement of anything - they are what makes the budget divide into 42 slots exactly at scale 1.0, and they came off THIS column because it is the only one of the four with slack against its own stated range (realistic maximum 230, text budget 244). See _horizontal_budget. A planet name is a star name plus a numeral; s_star.name is str15 (star.py:35) and a player can type all fifteen when renaming a home star (namestar.cpp:262). Fifteen wide glyphs render 336 px - but the widest of the 54 stars in the running reference galaxy is 'Draconis IV' at 124 px, and a realistic 15-character name is 190 to 230 ('New Constantine V' is 208). 330 was chosen to hold 336 and cost 90 px of the shared budget for a name nobody types. This was rejected once at 230 because the render showed the name overprinting the track - under LEFT alignment. Right alignment sends overflow LEFT into pad_x, where nothing is drawn, so that render no longer applies and the trade re-opened. The structural maximum is now the ELLIPSIS case, not the reservation: a name that outruns the column plus pad_x is cut with 'ellipsis' rather than reserved for. It degrades visibly in the one case it cannot hold and costs nothing in every case it can.
list._detail_note: The second line under the colony name; see _hd_extension for why it is marked. Substitution is a replace, not str.format (decision 37), so a stray brace in a translated string cannot raise inside the render path; an unknown placeholder is left standing rather than swallowed, which is visible instead of silent. {pops}/{max_pop} is the pair the original prints - colsum.cpp:1199 passes colony->n_pops and Planet_Max_Population_For_Player_ into E_Strings_(74).
list._climates_note: Indexed by s_colony.climate (offset 226), the PLANET_CLIMATE enum at orion2_consts.h:362-374. THE COLONY'S FIELD, NOT THE PLANET'S, and that is source-backed rather than reasoned: Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ takes climate_idx = colony->climate (colsum.cpp:1167) and indexes the same table. The wording is here rather than in code so a translation replaces it without touching a renderer (decision 15). PROVENANCE, ONE HOME: the original maps climate to string in exactly one place, estrings.cpp:204-213, which fills MOX::_planet_climate_string[] from the enum. Every screen that shows a climate indexes THAT table (colsum.cpp:1199, colland.cpp:40, colsysdi.cpp:165, plntsum.cpp:151, mainpups.cpp:348). This note used to list the ten ESTR ids it maps to; they were checked against that table on 1 September 2026 and all ten agreed, and they were then REMOVED - a second copy of a table that agrees today is the screen-ID-map failure waiting, and a pointer cannot drift. Order is load-bearing: it is the enum, not an alphabetical or quality ranking.
list._name_gap_note: Gutter between the right edge of the name block and the first slot of the track. Taken out of name_width, NOT out of the shared budget - the track keeps its 22 px slot. Without it the right-aligned name ends on exactly the pixel the first square begins on, and the two read as a collision rather than as an alignment; the first render after right-aligning showed exactly that. It also sets how much overflow the column can absorb. The gap comes OUT of name_width, so the name ends at name_width - name_gap and may then grow left across pad_x: 236 - 14 + 22 = 244 px of room before the clip has anything to do, at EVERY resolution. This is the floor of the gutter and not the whole of it: the renderer adds the budget's per-resolution remainder on the same side, so the measured gap between the name and the first slot is name_gap plus up to 30 px more at small scales. That addition moves the bar, never the clip. That is BELOW the structural maximum of 336, and deliberately - the ellipsis is the answer to 336, not the reservation. It is above the realistic maximum of 230, which is the case the column is sized for.
list._hd_extension: HD EXTENSION. The 'detail' line under each colony name - climate and pops/max_pop - is drawn PER ROW. The original prints it for the SELECTED colony only, into the bottom-left scan box at native (13, 354, 80, 88): COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ (colsum.cpp:1155) formats ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(74) and squeezes it into that rect, guarded by _g_colony_n != -1. The rows carry a name and nothing else. Showing it on every row makes comparable what the original could only show one at a time - the same family as the allocation bar, and not something MOO2 chose against but something its screen had no room for. It is also a SUBSET: the original's line carries planet size, gravity, mineral class and growth as well, and those are not drawn. Marked here, in colonylist.py, in v3_projektstatus.md and in a smoke check.
list._building_column_note: 190 reference px, and it is a HARD width. Transcribed from BILL::Squeeze_Print_Formatted_Paragraph_(0x200, y, 0x55, 0x16) at colsum.cpp:621 - x 512, width 85, max height 22, of 640. 85/640 is 13.3 %, which is 190 of 1408. WHY IT IS A RESERVATION: _Squeeze_Print_Paragraph_ (bill.cpp:147) passes width straight into get_height(width, text) and loops on max_height >= height. The text is WRAPPED into the width and the HEIGHT is what is made to fit; width never moves, and there is no truncation branch in that function at all. TWO LINES, AND THE ORIGINAL BUDGETS TWO IN THE SAME BOX: max height 0x16 = 22 goes into a row whose pitch is 31 (buy_btn_y_coords steps 35, 65, 96, 128 ...), so that box is two thirds of its row and holds more than one line of its own font. The two-line column is the same PLACE as the original's, not just the same technique used elsewhere. TRANSCRIBED BEHAVIOUR, NOT MECHANISM: wrap into the width, reduce size until it fits, never truncate. The original's first squeeze step narrows the SPACE GLYPH (font_style_widths[32]--), a bitmap-font trick with no Aldrich equivalent; its third steps between discrete bitmap faces. build_font_min is the floor, and the text is drawn whole even there - the original prints the paragraph regardless once it runs out of things to shrink. A previous pass measured this as widest string, one line, full font and got 311 px, nearly twice as much; all three of those constraints are ones the original never imposes.
list._buy_note: TRANSCRIBED IN POSITION, DEVIATES TWICE IN FORM. The original adds one per row at native x=599 (colsum.cpp:302, _list_buy_fields[10], buy_btn_y_coords), to the right of the producing text, as a Locked_Button_Field_ or a hidden field depending on Colony_Can_Buy_Product_0_. That is transcribed. DEVIATION 1: the LABEL. E_Strings_(12) is empty, so 'Buy' is a word this project chose; it lives here per decision 15. DEVIATION 2: drawing TEXT AT ALL. The original's control is a SPRITE - _anims[i + 11] supplies the artwork, which is why its label string can be empty. A text button is a different object, not a translation of that one, and it is drawn this way because the sprite is in the player's LBX and is not shipped. Naming only the label would leave the larger deviation unmarked. can_buy on the row decides whether it is drawn; nothing sends a click yet.
list._width_condition_note: MARKED. squeeze_lines reduces the size until BOTH the height and the WIDTH fit. _Squeeze_Print_Paragraph_ loops on height alone, and fmtpara.cpp offers Get_Formatted_Paragraph_Max_Width_ beside the height function without calling it - so the question was whether the original lets an over-wide token overflow. It does not. _Print_Formatted_Paragraph_ places a character when char_x_end <= right_limit_x || line_started != 0 (fmtpara.cpp:567); line_started is 1 at line start and 0 after the first character (:540, :572), so the first character is placed unconditionally and every later one must fit. When one does not, Return_To_Last_Break_() is tried - breaks are recorded only at spaces, tabs and soft hyphens (:723, :731) - but _para_p->str-- runs whether it succeeded or not and the line ends (:583-587). A token with no break inside it is therefore BROKEN MID-TOKEN, and the paragraph never exceeds the width. Height alone is sufficient BECAUSE the width can never be exceeded. So: the GUARANTEE (no ink past the width, nothing truncated) is a TRANSCRIPTION and our width condition delivers it. The MEANS is a DEVIATION: the original character-wraps the token, we reduce the size and keep it whole. Visible, therefore marked. The reason is that the over-wide token here is a ship design name - user-typed data whose exact form is the point - and a hyphen-less mid-word break that reads as wrapping in a five-pixel face at 640x480 reads as corruption at HD.
list._row_height_note: 58, and the number is the ORIGINAL'S WINDOW plus the overflow line, not a look. COLSUM::_list_col[10] holds ten rows and Update_Col_List_ (colsum.cpp:348) fills exactly that many, so ten is what the original shows at once; at 62 px the HD panel held NINE, because list_area is 619 reference px and pad_y takes 14, leaving 605 and 605/62 = 9. 60 WOULD FIT TEN AND WAS STILL WRONG: 10 x 60 = 600 leaves 5 px, and the '{count} more not shown' line is about 15, so it would have been clamped back over the last row it is there to account for. The two features fight for the same pixels and the arithmetic has to hold BOTH: 10 x 58 = 580 leaves 25, which the line fits in. That is why this is 58 and not 60, and it is the kind of interaction a change made on one of the two alone gets wrong silently - the smoke test caught it. WHY row_height AND NOT list_area: the box is derived from the frame artwork by frame_holes.py (decision 3), and moving it by hand slides the content out from under its hole. Growing the panel means redrawing the frame, which is an artwork decision with its own reasons; taking four pixels off a row is not. bar_height came down with it, 34 to 30, to keep the band 'No Farming' is drawn in exactly as wide: row_height minus bar_height is 28 either way, split 14 above and 14 below by centring the bar, and the label renders 88x14. Leaving bar_height at 34 would have left 12 px for a 14 px label - see _no_farming_note, where that band is the whole argument.
list._frame_bleed_note: NOTED, NOT FIXED: the frame's metal edge overlaps the first three or four pixels of list_area on both sides, so the box's USABLE width is a little narrower than its width. Measured on 3 September 2026 while the preview's invariant check was comparing whole row bands: it reported 310 differing pixels between two renderings of the same colony, every one of them at x 0..3 or 1405..1407, and all of them frame artwork that legitimately differs between one y and another rather than anything to do with the list. IT IS HARMLESS TODAY. Nothing is drawn in that strip - pad_x is 22 px on each side and the row starts inside it - so the overlap costs nothing and no column is being clipped. IT IS WRITTEN DOWN BECAUSE THE BOX IS DERIVED FROM THE ARTWORK. frame_holes.py reads the transparent holes out of frame.png (decision 3), so the box is exactly the hole and the hole is exactly what the drawing left open - which means the bleed is not an error anywhere, and the next person to measure ink against the box edge will find pixels they did not put there and have to work out why. This is that answer, ahead of the question. Anything comparing rendered pixels against list_area should inset by pad_x or work in the track's own coordinates, which is what colony_list_preview.colony_track_rect does and says.

words._note: THE WORD LISTS THE SCAN BOX SUBSTITUTES, and they are OUR OWN WORDING, not the game's bytes. The original fills four tables - MOX::_planet_size_string, _mineral_class_string and _planet_gravity_string at estrings.cpp:155-169, _planet_climate_string at estrings.cpp:204-213 - and every entry is an ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(id) call, so the strings themselves come from the player's own estrings.lbx, loaded at runtime and one file per language (estrings.cpp, Load_E_Strings_). They are not in the orion2re source, they are not shipped, and nothing here extracts them - the same absence that leaves the building column empty and gave the Buy button an invented label. So these are English words this project chose to match what the game prints, and they live here rather than in a renderer so a translation replaces them without touching code (decision 15). ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING: each list is indexed by its enum and is not a ranking - PLANET_SIZE at orion2_consts.h:392-397, MINERAL_RESOURCE at :328-333, PLANET_GRAVITY at :377-380. THE RULE, and it is a rule and not three separate decisions: A VALUE CARRIES NO PREFIX, BECAUSE THE LABEL CARRIES IT. This panel is a table of label-and-value pairs and the original's box is one run-on paragraph, so a word that reads correctly there reads twice here. The source draws the distinction more finely than 'our list is wrong' does. MINERALS: colland.cpp:60-62 puts the table value into its own format string, E_Strings_(0x176), and the word 'Mineral' belongs to that FORMAT - the table holds 'Rich', which is what this list holds, and 'Mineral Rich' here would render as MINERALS Mineral Rich. GRAVITY: colland.cpp:65 prints the table entry with no format at all, so the full string 'Normal Gravity' really is in the table - and copying it verbatim would render as GRAVITY Normal Gravity, the same fault from the other direction. Both lists therefore carry the bare quality and the label supplies the noun. 'Normal G' was neither: it was the enum name (PLANET_GRAVITY_NORMAL_G) in title case, which is how a list derived from identifiers rather than from the screen goes wrong. SECOND SOURCE, and it is what corrected this: the original's own scan box read 'Huge Desert / Normal Gravity / Mineral Rich / Population (4/8) / +63k' on 3 September 2026, in the first --live --native side-by-side this project ever ran. Before that the planet description for Ixion II on 31 August had confirmed 'Small Ocean, Normal Gravity, Mineral Abundant' and the direction of all three enums. CLIMATE IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. It already has a home at list.climates, with its own provenance note, and is read from there by the row renderer and by the output panel alike. A second copy that agrees today is the screen-ID-map failure waiting; a smoke check asserts the ten climate words appear in exactly one of the two blocks.

output._note: output_panel is a TRANSCRIPTION of the original's bottom-left scan box (decision 43 was withdrawn; see screen.py). Two calls fill that box for the SELECTED colony, both in COLSUM::Draw_Colony_Scan_Info_ (colsum.cpp:1155), which is guarded by _g_colony_n != -1: a formatted paragraph at native (13, 354, 80, 88) that substitutes SEVEN values into ESTRINGS::E_Strings_(74) (colsum.cpp:1196-1206), and a column of production rows plus morale at native x 106 (colsum.cpp:1171-1176). The wording of every label here is ours and lives in this file (decision 15); substitution is a replace and never str.format (decision 37), so a stray brace in a translated label cannot raise inside the render path and an unknown placeholder is left standing rather than swallowed.
output._deviation_note: TWO DEVIATIONS, both one line in this file away from being undone. (1) EACH PRODUCTION ROW IS ONE NUMBER, and the original's is several. COLDRAW::Draw_Colony_Prod_Both_ (coldraw.cpp:36) draws the net value beside imports (coldraw.cpp:46), pollution for industry (coldraw.cpp:56), and a shortage computed as maintenance minus imports minus production (coldraw.cpp:61), all as tens-and-units sprites. This panel prints colony->production[i] (coldraw.cpp:60) and nothing else, so it is a SUBSET of that row rather than a smaller drawing of it. (2) MORALE IS A NUMBER HERE AND A ROW OF ICONS THERE. COLDRAW::Draw_Info_Morale_Both_ draws abs(morale / 2) sprites, capped at 20, in one of two artworks depending on the sign. The sprites are in the player's LBX and are not shipped, which is the same reason the Buy control is a text button - see list._buy_note, where the same trade is made and marked. What IS transcribed is the value (the signed halving, C truncation toward zero) and the Unification rule below. A THIRD DEVIATION IS GONE, 3 September 2026: BC was not drawn, on the reading that the panel showed 'food, industry and research'. The original draws four. Its loop is `i < ECON_COUNT` and ECON_COUNT is 4 (orion2_consts.h:123), and the GEOMETRY settles it independently of the constant: y_pos starts at 349 and steps 18 (colsum.cpp:1170-1173), giving 349, 367, 385, 403, and morale is drawn at 421 (colsum.cpp:1176) - one step further on, which leaves room for exactly four rows above it and not three. The BC row is now drawn and the smoke check that asserted its absence is gone with it.
output._morale_note: UNDER UNIFICATION THE ORIGINAL DRAWS NO MORALE AT ALL. Draw_Info_Morale_Both_ sets its count to 0 when the owner's traits[TRAIT_CURRENT_GOVERNMENT] is GOVERNMENT_UNIFICATION or above (6 and 7, orion2_consts.h:199-200; the trait index is 0, orion2_consts.h:949). Transcribed: the row renders `hidden_value` rather than a zero, because a drawn 0 is a claim that morale is neutral and the original is claiming that morale does not apply. The trait comes from the verified s_player spec (traits @2308).
output._growth_note: The sum of s_colony.pop_growth[10] (offset 200), which is what colsum.cpp:1179-1182 accumulates into total_growth and passes to E_Strings_(74). THE k IS A UNIT, NOT A DECORATION. MOO2 counts population in thousands, so the number is thousands of colonists and the original prints it that way: its scan box read '+63k' on 3 September 2026, in the first --live --native side-by-side. The sign is explicit for the same reason the sidebar's Income and Food carry one - it is a net flow and a negative one means the colony is shrinking - and it comes from colonyempire.format_value, which is the one home for that rule. The 'k' is wording and lives here in the template (decision 15). WHAT THIS DOES NOT DO: divide, round or scale. The engine's number is printed as the engine's number; only the unit that was always implied is now written down. Inventing a division to turn it into whole colonists would be reading a meaning into a field whose meaning still rests on the header's name alone. colsum.cpp:1180 also sums pop_roundoff[10] into total_roundoff and then never passes it to anything - not transcribed, because there is nothing to transcribe. The original colours a negative growth as well (colsum.cpp:1187-1190), which needs the inline attribute machinery and is not done here.
output._offsets_note: MEANING, NOT LAYOUT. s_colony and s_planet_data are verified specs, which fixes where every member sits and how wide it is and says nothing about what its values mean (decision 23). SIX OF THE SEVEN SCAN VALUES NOW AGREE WITH THE ORIGINAL'S OWN BOX. Read for Sadak I on 3 September 2026 in the second --live --native side-by-side, with both halves on the same sort key: the original printed 'Huge Desert / Normal Gravity / Mineral Rich / Population (4/8) / +63k' and this panel showed Huge, Desert, Normal, Rich, 4/8 and +63k. That closes growth, which had rested on the header's name alone; size, climate, gravity_class, mineral_class and n_pops had already been read against the original's planet description for Ixion II on 31 August, and max_pop is computed from them rather than read. MORALE IS THE ONE THAT DID NOT FALL, and the obstacle is an input capability and not the data. The comparison needs the original's box pointed at a colony with non-zero morale; _g_colony_n moves on HOVER (colsum.cpp:880-890), the Extension API cannot inject a hover, every click that lands on a row does something else instead, and the game's window is hidden while the API is on (platform.cpp:1379) so it cannot be hovered by hand. A save in which the colony the original is already scanning has non-zero morale settles it without any of that.
output._empty_note: EMPTY, and that is the point. With no colony selected the panel draws NOTHING - no labels, no dashes, no zeroes. The original's box is guarded by `_g_colony_n != -1` (colsum.cpp:1165) and simply is not drawn, and a zero would be a value where the original has an absence. Put a string here to have it drawn centred instead; a smoke check asserts the panel puts no ink on an empty selection while the shipped value is empty.
output._rows_note: ELEVEN VALUES, and the split follows the original's own two halves. LEFT is the scan paragraph: the seven values E_Strings_(74) carries - planet size, climate, gravity class, mineral class, n_pops, the computed maximum and growth (colsum.cpp:1198-1205) - in six rows, because the original prints n_pops and the maximum as one pair and so does this. RIGHT is the production column: all four ECON values (colsum.cpp:1171-1174 at native x 106, y 349 stepping 18) with morale under them (colsum.cpp:1176, y 421), which is the same order and the same grouping the original draws at native x 106. Morale is the eleventh row and is not one of the ten scan-and-production values: it is a count of sprites there, and a number here only because the sprites are not ours to ship. THREE OF THE SEVEN ARE ALSO IN THE ROW. climate, n_pops and max_pop are drawn per row as well (list._hd_extension), and that is not a duplication to clean up: the per-row line is the HD EXTENSION and THIS is the original's own box, which prints all seven for one colony. Removing them here would make the transcription a subset in order to tidy an extension.
output._geometry_note: TUNED AGAINST THE PICTURE, not against a rule. output_panel is 464 x 201 reference px and the fuller column holds six rows, so the pitch is (201 - 2*pad_y - 5*row_gap) / 6 and a column is (464 - 2*pad_x) / 2 = 216. column_gap 34 is the one number that came out of looking: at the first render it was 12, and 'Huge GROWTH' and 'Ultra Poor RESEARCH' read as single phrases because the left column's right-aligned value ended a few pixels from the right column's left-aligned label. Every number in that render was correct and the panel was unreadable, which is the failure mode the fundament's 'render it and look at it' rule exists for. Two smoke checks hold the result, both measured by rendering per decision 30. (a) The GUTTER between the columns must be at least one em of the value font - the rule the 34 was measured against and the one the 12 broke. (b) Within a column, each row's label must clear the widest value THAT ROW can show by at least one em of the label font. Per row, and that matters: pairing the widest label in the panel with the widest value in the panel asserts a collision that cannot happen, because POPULATION never prints 'Ultra Poor', and it failed at 1280x720 on exactly that imaginary pair. The real tightest is MINERALS against 'Ultra Poor', 21 px to spare at scale 1.0. Both at twelve resolutions.
